definitions.explanation: An electric charge that builds up on the surface of objects, commonly experienced as a small shock when touching metal objects or other people, especially in dry winter weather.

examples.japanese: {静電気|せいでんき}でバチッときた。
{冬|ふゆ}は{静電気|せいでんき}が{起|お}きやすい。
examples.english: Static electricity occurs easily in winter.

examples.japanese: ドアノブに{触|さわ}るたびに{静電気|せいでんき}が{走|はし}るので{困|こま}っている。
examples.english: I'm bothered by getting a static shock every time I touch a doorknob.

notes: Combines {静|せい} (still, static) + {電気|でんき} (electricity). Very commonly discussed in Japan during the dry winter months. Common collocations: {静電気|せいでんき}が{起|お}きる (static builds up), {静電気|せいでんき}が{走|はし}る (a static shock runs through), {静電気|せいでんき}{防止|ぼうし} (anti-static), {静電気|せいでんき}{除去|じょきょ} (static removal). Products like {静電気|せいでんき}{防止|ぼうし}スプレー (anti-static spray) are popular in Japan.
